claim: P-Rex1 is abundantly expressed in neutrophils.
source: PIP3-dependent Rac exchanger 1 (P-Rex1) is abundantly expressed in neutrophils and plays central roles in chemotaxis and cancer metastasis by serving as a guanine-nucleotide exchange factor (GEF) for Rac.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established fact about P-Rex1 expression.

claim: P-Rex1 plays central roles in chemotaxis and cancer metastasis.
source: PIP3-dependent Rac exchanger 1 (P-Rex1) is abundantly expressed in neutrophils and plays central roles in chemotaxis and cancer metastasis by serving as a guanine-nucleotide exchange factor (GEF) for Rac.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established fact about P-Rex1 function.

claim: P-Rex1 serves as a guanine-nucleotide exchange factor (GEF) for Rac.
source: PIP3-dependent Rac exchanger 1 (P-Rex1) is abundantly expressed in neutrophils and plays central roles in chemotaxis and cancer metastasis by serving as a guanine-nucleotide exchange factor (GEF) for Rac.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established fact about P-Rex1 function.

claim: P-Rex1 is synergistically activated by PIP3 and heterotrimeric Gβγ subunits.
source: The enzyme is synergistically activated by PIP3 and heterotrimeric Gβγ subunits, but mechanistic details remain poorly understood.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established fact about P-Rex1 activation.

claim: Ins(1,3,4,5)P4 (IP4) inhibits P-Rex1 activity.
source: While investigating the regulation of P-Rex1 by PIP3, we discovered that Ins(1,3,4,5)P4 (IP4) inhibits P-Rex1 activity and induces large decreases in backbone dynamics in diverse regions of the protein.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 1D.

claim: IP4 induces large decreases in backbone dynamics in diverse regions of P-Rex1.
source: While investigating the regulation of P-Rex1 by PIP3, we discovered that Ins(1,3,4,5)P4 (IP4) inhibits P-Rex1 activity and induces large decreases in backbone dynamics in diverse regions of the protein.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the abstract and supported by HDX-MS data in Figure 1.

claim: In the P-Rex1·IP4 complex, the pleckstrin homology (PH) domain occludes the active site of the Dbl homology (DH) domain.
source: Cryo-electron microscopy analysis of the P-Rex1·IP4 complex revealed a conformation wherein the pleckstrin homology (PH) domain occludes the active site of the Dbl homology (DH) domain.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the abstract and supported by cryo-EM structure in Figure 2.

claim: The occluded conformation of P-Rex1 is stabilized by interactions between the first DEP domain (DEP1) and the DH domain.
source: This configuration is stabilized by interactions between the first DEP domain (DEP1) and the DH domain and between the PH domain and a 4-helix bundle (4HB) subdomain that extends from the C-terminal domain of P-Rex1.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the abstract and supported by cryo-EM structure in Figure 2 and Figure 3.

claim: The occluded conformation of P-Rex1 is stabilized by interactions between the PH domain and a 4-helix bundle (4HB) subdomain that extends from the C-terminal domain of P-Rex1.
source: This configuration is stabilized by interactions between the first DEP domain (DEP1) and the DH domain and between the PH domain and a 4-helix bundle (4HB) subdomain that extends from the C-terminal domain of P-Rex1.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the abstract and supported by cryo-EM structure in Figure 2.

claim: Disruption of the DH–DEP1 interface in a DH/PH-DEP1 fragment enhanced activity.
source: Disruption of the DH–DEP1 interface in a DH/PH-DEP1 fragment enhanced activity and led to a more extended conformation in solution, whereas mutations that constrain the occluded conformation led to decreased GEF activity.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the abstract and supported by GEF activity data in Figure 3C.

claim: Disruption of the DH–DEP1 interface in a DH/PH-DEP1 fragment led to a more extended conformation in solution.
source: Disruption of the DH–DEP1 interface in a DH/PH-DEP1 fragment enhanced activity and led to a more extended conformation in solution, whereas mutations that constrain the occluded conformation led to decreased GEF activity.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the abstract and supported by SAXS data in Figure 3E and F.

claim: Mutations that constrain the occluded conformation led to decreased GEF activity.
source: Disruption of the DH–DEP1 interface in a DH/PH-DEP1 fragment enhanced activity and led to a more extended conformation in solution, whereas mutations that constrain the occluded conformation led to decreased GEF activity.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the abstract and supported by GEF activity data in Figure 3C.

claim: Variants of full-length P-Rex1 in which the DH–DEP1 and PH–4HB interfaces were disturbed exhibited enhanced activity during chemokine-induced cell migration.
source: Variants of full-length P-Rex1 in which the DH–DEP1 and PH–4HB interfaces were disturbed exhibited enhanced activity during chemokine-induced cell migration, confirming that the observed structure represents the autoinhibited state in living cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the abstract and supported by cell migration data in Figure 5.

claim: The observed structure represents the autoinhibited state in living cells.
source: Variants of full-length P-Rex1 in which the DH–DEP1 and PH–4HB interfaces were disturbed exhibited enhanced activity during chemokine-induced cell migration, confirming that the observed structure represents the autoinhibited state in living cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the cell migration data in Figure 5 showing that disrupting the interfaces increases activity.

claim: Interactions with PIP3-containing liposomes led to disruption of the DH–DEP1 and PH–4HB interfaces.
source: Interactions with PIP3-containing liposomes led to disruption of these interfaces and increased dynamics protein-wide.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the abstract and supported by HDX-MS data in Figure 6.

claim: Interactions with PIP3-containing liposomes increased dynamics protein-wide.
source: Interactions with PIP3-containing liposomes led to disruption of these interfaces and increased dynamics protein-wide.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the abstract and supported by HDX-MS data in Figure 6.

claim: Inositol phosphates such as IP4 help to inhibit basal P-Rex1 activity in neutrophils, similar to their inhibitory effects on phosphatidylinositol-3-kinase.
source: Our results further suggest that inositol phosphates such as IP4 help to inhibit basal P-Rex1 activity in neutrophils, similar to their inhibitory effects on phosphatidylinositol-3-kinase.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data and comparison to known effects on PI3K.

claim: P-Rex1 is comprised of a catalytic Dbl homology (DH) domain followed by a pleckstrin homology (PH) domain, two DEP domains (DEP1 and DEP2), two PDZ domains (PDZ1 and PDZ2), and a C-terminal inositol polyphosphate-4-phosphatase-like (IP4P) domain.
source: The protein is comprised of a catalytic Dbl homology (DH) domain followed by a pleckstrin homology (PH) domain, two DEP domains (DEP1 and DEP2), two PDZ domains (PDZ1 and PDZ2), and a C-terminal inositol polyphosphate-4-phosphatase-like (IP4P) domain (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: IP4 inhibits PIP3-mediated activation of P-Rex1 with an IC50 value of 1.4 μM.
source: Using an in vitro GEF activity assay on soluble Cdc42 in the presence of liposomes, we observed that IP4 inhibits PIP3-mediated activation of P-Rex1 with an IC50 value of 1.4 μM (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Competition with IP4 was not observed with Ins(1,4,5)P3.
source: Competition was not observed with Ins(1,4,5)P3, indicating that inhibition is dependent on the 3-phosphate, which is critical for PIP3 binding to the P-Rex1 PH domain (Cash et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an experimental observation.

claim: Inhibition by IP4 is dependent on the 3-phosphate, which is critical for PIP3 binding to the P-Rex1 PH domain.
source: Competition was not observed with Ins(1,4,5)P3, indicating that inhibition is dependent on the 3-phosphate, which is critical for PIP3 binding to the P-Rex1 PH domain (Cash et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an interpretation of the data with a citation to prior work.

claim: IP4 did not affect the activity of the P-Rex1 DH/PH or DH/PH-DEP1 fragments.
source: However, IP4 did not affect the activity of the P-Rex1 DH/PH or DH/PH-DEP1 fragments (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: IP4 inhibits P-Rex1 allosterically.
source: Collectively, these results indicated that IP4 inhibits P-Rex1 allosterically and that this inhibition is dependent on long-range interactions between the regions shown to be protected by IP4 in the Gβγ-binding scaffold (DEP2-PDZ1-PDZ2-IP4P) and in the DH/PH-DEP1 module.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing that IP4 does not affect DH/PH or DH/PH-DEP1 fragments but does affect full-length P-Rex1.

claim: IP4 inhibition is dependent on long-range interactions between the regions shown to be protected by IP4 in the Gβγ-binding scaffold (DEP2-PDZ1-PDZ2-IP4P) and in the DH/PH-DEP1 module.
source: Collectively, these results indicated that IP4 inhibits P-Rex1 allosterically and that this inhibition is dependent on long-range interactions between the regions shown to be protected by IP4 in the Gβγ-binding scaffold (DEP2-PDZ1-PDZ2-IP4P) and in the DH/PH-DEP1 module.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the HDX-MS data in Figure 1 and the activity data.

claim: The structure of the P-Rex1·IP4 complex was determined at an average resolution of 4.1 Å.
source: We next collected much larger datasets on the P-Rex1·IP4 complex using a Krios transmission electron microscope and determined the structure of this complex at an average resolution of 4.1 Å (Figure 2A and B, Table 1, and Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Table 1 and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The P-Rex1·IP4 sample exhibited a preferred orientation on grids.
source: Similar to the P-Rex1–Gβγ complex (Cash et al., 2019), this sample exhibited a preferred orientation on grids, necessitating the addition of data collected on a tilted sample (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A and C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an observation during cryo-EM data collection.

claim: The 3D reconstruction of P-Rex1·IP4 clearly shows the Gβγ-binding core, composed of DEP2, PDZ1, PDZ2, and the majority of the IP4P domain.
source: The resulting 3D reconstruction clearly shows the Gβγ-binding core, composed of DEP2, PDZ1, PDZ2, and the majority of the IP4P domain, from which there are two extensions of density that contact one another to form a loop-like structure (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 2D.

claim: One extension of the P-Rex1·IP4 structure corresponds to a large insertion in the IP4P domain that contains IP4-stabilized regions.
source: One extension corresponds to a large insertion in the IP4P domain that contains IP4-stabilized regions (Figure 1) and that was disordered in the P-Rex1–Gβγ complex (Cash et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 1 and a citation to prior work.

claim: The ordered elements of the IP4P domain insertion form a long 4-helix bundle (4HB) most similar in fold to focal adhesion targeting (FAT) domains.
source: The ordered elements of the insertion form a long 4-helix bundle (4HB) most similar in fold to focal adhesion targeting (FAT) domains (Hayashi et al., 2002), which are found in other peripheral membrane proteins involved in cell adhesion and migration.
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation to prior work on FAT domains.

claim: FAT domains are found in other peripheral membrane proteins involved in cell adhesion and migration.
source: The ordered elements of the insertion form a long 4-helix bundle (4HB) most similar in fold to focal adhesion targeting (FAT) domains (Hayashi et al., 2002), which are found in other peripheral membrane proteins involved in cell adhesion and migration.
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation to prior work.

claim: IP4 is observed bound to the PH domain PIP3-binding site in the P-Rex1·IP4 structure.
source: Based on its distinct shape, the PH domain (Cash et al., 2016) was fit into density along the side of the 4HB. Here, IP4 is observed bound to the PH domain PIP3-binding site (Figure 2B–D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2B–D.

claim: The relative positions of the DH and PH domains mandate a severe bend in the helix connecting the DH and PH domains.
source: The relative positions of the DH and PH domains mandate a severe bend in the helix connecting the DH and PH domains (Figure 2A and B), resulting in a jack-knifed configuration of the DH/PH module that blocks access to the GTPase binding site on the DH domain.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: The jack-knifed configuration of the DH/PH module blocks access to the GTPase binding site on the DH domain.
source: The relative positions of the DH and PH domains mandate a severe bend in the helix connecting the DH and PH domains (Figure 2A and B), resulting in a jack-knifed configuration of the DH/PH module that blocks access to the GTPase binding site on the DH domain.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: The conformation of the P-Rex1 Gβγ-binding core is essentially the same as in the P-Rex1–Gβγ complex (RMSD deviation of 1.1 Å for 701 Cα atoms).
source: Overall, the conformation of the P-Rex1 Gβγ-binding core is essentially the same as in the P-Rex1–Gβγ complex (RMSD deviation of 1.1 Å for 701 Cα atoms).
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a comparison to prior structural work.

claim: The PH–4HB interface primarily involves the β1/β2 and β5/β6 loops of the PH domain.
source: The contact between the PH domain and the 4HB is primarily mediated via the β1 and β2 strands and β5/β6 loop of the PH domain (Figure 2C and D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2C and D.

claim: The β1/β2 and β5/β6 loops of the PH domain were previously shown to be involved in protein-protein interactions in crystal structures.
source: In all previous crystal structures including the P-Rex1 PH domain, this same surface formed extensive protein–protein lattice contacts (Cash et al., 2016; Lucato et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citations to prior work.

claim: The residues directly involved in the PH–4HB interface are among the most strongly protected in the presence of IP4 as measured by HDX-MS.
source: The residues directly involved in the interface are among the most strongly protected in the presence of IP4 as measured by HDX-MS (Figure 1A–C, Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1A–C and Figure 4A.

claim: The PH domain β3/β4 loop is a nonspecific anionic membrane-binding loop.
source: The PH domain β3/β4 loop, which we previously showed to be a nonspecific anionic membrane-binding loop, remains unstructured and is situated near a loop at the tip of the 4HB that is also unstructured (residues 1109–1209, Figure 2C) and contains known phosphorylation sites, some of which regulate activity (Barber et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation to prior work.

claim: The loop at the tip of the 4HB (residues 1109–1209) contains known phosphorylation sites, some of which regulate activity.
source: The PH domain β3/β4 loop, which we previously showed to be a nonspecific anionic membrane-binding loop, remains unstructured and is situated near a loop at the tip of the 4HB that is also unstructured (residues 1109–1209, Figure 2C) and contains known phosphorylation sites, some of which regulate activity (Barber et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation to prior work.

claim: At the PH–4HB interface, surface hydrophobic residues Leu279 and Ile286 on the PH β1 and β2 strands and Tyr353 on the β5/β6 loop interact with a surface of 4HB including Tyr1096 and His1224.
source: At the interface, surface hydrophobic residues Leu279 and Ile286 on the PH β1 and β2 strands and Tyr353 on the β5/β6 loop interact with a surface of 4HB including Tyr1096 and His1224 (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Charge complementarity is formed between Lys302 in the PH domain and Asp1216 in 4HB.
source: Charge complementarity is formed between Lys302 in the PH domain and Asp1216 in 4HB, and between the 1-phosphate of IP4 and Lys1217.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an observation from the structure.

claim: Charge complementarity is formed between the 1-phosphate of IP4 and Lys1217.
source: Charge complementarity is formed between Lys302 in the PH domain and Asp1216 in 4HB, and between the 1-phosphate of IP4 and Lys1217.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an observation from the structure.

claim: IP4 does not make direct contact with the 4HB.
source: Otherwise, IP4 does not make direct contact with the 4HB.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an observation from the structure.

claim: Different PH domain ligands uniquely perturb the conformation of the β1 and β2 strands and β5/β6 loop in the PH domain.
source: However, because different PH domain ligands uniquely perturb the conformation of these regions in the PH domain (Cash et al., 2016), IP4 could indirectly stabilize this interface by trapping the β1 and β2 strands and β5/β6 loop in a conformation with higher affinity for 4HB.
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation to prior work.

claim: IP4 could indirectly stabilize the PH–4HB interface by trapping the β1 and β2 strands and β5/β6 loop in a conformation with higher affinity for 4HB.
source: However, because different PH domain ligands uniquely perturb the conformation of these regions in the PH domain (Cash et al., 2016), IP4 could indirectly stabilize this interface by trapping the β1 and β2 strands and β5/β6 loop in a conformation with higher affinity for 4HB.
evidence: This is a hypothesis stated in the results section based on prior work and the current structure.

claim: DH domain residues Leu173, Leu177, and Leu178 form a hydrophobic interface with DEP1 residues Ile409, Ile457, Leu466, and Ala469.
source: DH domain residues Leu173, Leu177, and Leu178 form a hydrophobic interface with DEP1 residues Ile409, Ile457, Leu466, and Ala469 (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Leu173 and Leu177 were previously noted to be conspicuously exposed in structures of the DH/PH tandem.
source: Leu173 and Leu177 were previously noted to be conspicuously exposed in structures of the DH/PH tandem (Cash et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation to prior work.

claim: The DEP1 domain stabilizes an inactive DH/PH tandem that is further stabilized by interaction with the 4HB of the IP4P domain.
source: Thus, the DEP1 domain stabilizes an inactive DH/PH tandem that is further stabilized by interaction with the 4HB of the IP4P domain.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the structural data.

claim: The domain organization of P-Rex1 with and without IP4 is very similar.
source: Overall, the domain organization is very similar, but there is an ~3° rotation of the Gβγ-binding core in the IP4 complex relative to the PH–4HB interface such that DEP1 and DEP2 move closer together.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a comparison to the structure without IP4 (PDB entry 7SYF).

claim: There is an ~3° rotation of the Gβγ-binding core in the IP4 complex relative to the PH–4HB interface such that DEP1 and DEP2 move closer together.
source: Overall, the domain organization is very similar, but there is an ~3° rotation of the Gβγ-binding core in the IP4 complex relative to the PH–4HB interface such that DEP1 and DEP2 move closer together.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a comparison to the structure without IP4 (PDB entry 7SYF).

claim: The binding of IP4 at the PH–4HB interface may drive the conformational change where DEP1 and DEP2 move closer together.
source: It is possible that the binding of IP4 at this interface drives this conformational change.
evidence: This is a hypothesis stated in the results section based on the structural comparison.

claim: The similarities between P-Rex1 ± IP4 suggest that the IP4-binding site in the PH domain is freely accessible in the autoinhibited state.
source: The similarities between P-Rex1 ± IP4 also suggest that the IP4-binding site in the PH domain is freely accessible in the autoinhibited state.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the structural comparison.

claim: PIP3 would not have access to the PH domain in the autoinhibited state because the 4HB domain would block binding to a membrane surface.
source: PIP3 would, however, not have access because the 4HB domain would block binding to a membrane surface.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the structural data.

claim: The DH/PH-DEP1 fragment is five- to tenfold less active (depending on assay conditions) than the DH/PH tandem alone.
source: This fragment is five- to tenfold less active (depending on assay conditions) than the DH/PH tandem alone (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C; Ravala et al., 2020), confirming a specific role for DEP1 in autoinhibition (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1C and a citation to prior work.

claim: The L173A variant of DH/PH-DEP1 had an ~2.5-fold higher activity than wild-type.
source: The L173A variant had an ~2.5-fold higher activity, whereas L177E and L178E exhibited four- to fivefold higher activity, similar to the activity of DH/PH without the DEP1 domain.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an experimental observation shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The L177E and L178E variants of DH/PH-DEP1 exhibited four- to fivefold higher activity than wild-type, similar to the activity of DH/PH without the DEP1 domain.
source: The L173A variant had an ~2.5-fold higher activity, whereas L177E and L178E exhibited four- to fivefold higher activity, similar to the activity of DH/PH without the DEP1 domain.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an experimental observation shown in Figure 3C.

claim: In the DEP1 domain, I409A and L466A mutations resulted in approximately two- and fourfold higher activity, respectively.
source: In the DEP1 domain, I409A and L466A mutations resulted in approximately two- and fourfold higher activity, respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an experimental observation shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The α1/α2 loop (residues 77–90) of the DH domain is disordered in the P-Rex1·IP4 structure.
source: The α1/α2 loop (residues 77–90) of the DH domain, although ordered in previous structures of DH/PH bound to GTPases (Cash et al., 2016; Lucato et al., 2015), is disordered in our structure (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citations to prior work and shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Modeling the DH domain from previous DH/PH crystal structures suggests that Lys89 and Arg78 would be close enough to form a bipartite ionic interaction with Glu456 in the DEP1 domain.
source: However, modeling the DH domain from previous DH/PH crystal structures suggests that Lys89 and Arg78 would be close enough to form a bipartite ionic interaction with Glu456 in the DEP1 domain.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a hypothesis based on modeling.

claim: The E456K variant of DH/PH-DEP1 was ~2.5-fold more active than wild-type.
source: Consistent with this hypothesis, the E456K variant was ~2.5-fold more active.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an experimental observation shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The A170K variant of DH/PH-DEP1 inhibited GEF activity by ~50%.
source: Surprisingly, one of the intended disruptive mutations, A170K, instead inhibited GEF activity by ~50% (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an experimental observation shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Lys170 in the DH domain could form complementary electrostatic interactions with Glu411 along with additional non-polar interactions with the backbone and side chains of residues 409, 411, and 412 in the DEP1 domain.
source: Based on the available structures, Lys170 in the DH domain could form complementary electrostatic interactions with Glu411 along with additional non-polar interactions with the backbone and side chains of residues 409, 411, and 412 in the DEP1 domain, thereby stabilizing the DH–DEP1 interface (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an interpretation of the structural data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Variants of DH/PH-DEP1 with increased activity had lower melting temperatures (Tm).
source: Indeed, variants with increased activity also had lower Tm values (Figure 3D, Table 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3D and Table 2.

claim: A170K, which was less active than WT DH/PH-DEP1, showed a higher Tm.
source: Conversely, A170K, which was less active than WT, showed a higher Tm.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3D and Table 2.

claim: DH/PH-DEP1 exhibited a more compact state with a smaller conformational landscape in solution relative to DH/PH.
source: In previous SAXS analyses, we observed that DH/PH-DEP1 exhibited a more compact state with a smaller conformational landscape in solution relative to DH/PH (Ravala et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation to prior work.

claim: Compared to WT DH/PH-DEP1, which had a radius of gyration (Rg) of 30 ± 0.3 Å, the L177E variant had an Rg of 31 ± 0.2 Å, suggestive of expansion.
source: Compared to WT DH/PH-DEP1, which had a radius of gyration (Rg) of 30 ± 0.3 Å, the L177E variant (the most active DH/PH-DEP1 variant tested) had an Rg of 31 ± 0.2 Å, suggestive of expansion (Figure 3E, Table 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3E and Table 3.

claim: Variants A170K and I409A had Rg values similar to that of WT DH/PH-DEP1.
source: Variants A170K and I409A had Rg values similar to that of WT.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Table 3.

claim: Kratky plots indicated that all the DH/PH-DEP1 samples had heterogeneous conformations.
source: Kratky plots indicated that all the samples had heterogeneous conformations (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2C.

claim: The S235C/M244C variant of DH/PH-DEP1 A170K decreased activity to nearly background in the oxidized but not the reduced state.
source: The S235C/M244C variant performed as expected, decreasing the activity of the A170K variant to nearly background in the oxidized but not the reduced state (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The M244C single mutant exhibited similar effects to S235C/M244C, suggesting that it forms disulfide bonds with cysteine(s) other than S235C.
source: However, the M244C single mutant exhibited similar effects, suggesting that it forms disulfide bonds with cysteine(s) other than S235C.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an interpretation of the data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The side chains of Cys200 and Cys234 are very close to that of M244C.
source: Indeed, the side chains of Cys200 and Cys234 are very close to that of M244C.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an observation from the structure.

claim: The K207C/E251C mutant was similar to S235C/M244C under oxidized conditions, but ~15-fold more active (similar to WT DH/PH levels) under reducing conditions.
source: The K207C/E251C mutant was similar to S235C/M244C under oxidized conditions, but ~15-fold more active (similar to WT DH/PH levels, see Figure 3C) under reducing conditions.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The K270C variant exhibited higher activity than A170K on its own under oxidizing conditions, but similar activity to all the variants except K207C/E251C when reduced.
source: The K270C variant, on the other hand, exhibited higher activity than A170K on its own under oxidizing conditions, but similar activity to all the variants except K207C/E251C when reduced.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Perturbation of contacts between the kinked segments of the α6-αN helix can have profound consequences on the activity of the DH/PH-DEP1 core.
source: Regardless, these data show that perturbation of contacts between the kinked segments of the α6-αN helix can have profound consequences on the activity of the DH/PH-DEP1 core.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the cysteine variant data.

claim: Mutations at the DH–DEP1 interface had a strong effect on full-length P-Rex1 activity in SRE luciferase-gene reporter assays.
source: Mutations at the DH–DEP1 interface had a strong effect on activity, with L177E and L466E (Figure 3A) exhibiting approximately tenfold and fourfold higher activity relative to WT, respectively (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 5A.

claim: L177E and L466E variants of full-length P-Rex1 exhibited approximately tenfold and fourfold higher activity relative to WT, respectively, in SRE luciferase-gene reporter assays.
source: Mutations at the DH–DEP1 interface had a strong effect on activity, with L177E and L466E (Figure 3A) exhibiting approximately tenfold and fourfold higher activity relative to WT, respectively (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Perturbation of the PH–4HB interface increased full-length P-Rex1 activity in SRE luciferase-gene reporter assays.
source: Perturbation of the PH–4HB interface (Figure 2D) also increased activity in that Y1096A was approximately fivefold more active than WT (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Y1096A variant of full-length P-Rex1 was approximately fivefold more active than WT in SRE luciferase-gene reporter assays.
source: Perturbation of the PH–4HB interface (Figure 2D) also increased activity in that Y1096A was approximately fivefold more active than WT (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 5A.

claim: L177E, L466E, and Y1096A variants of full-length P-Rex1 caused a significantly larger number of HeLa cells to migrate in response to CXCL12.
source: CXCL12-induced chemotaxis was dependent on the expression of P-Rex1 (Figure 5B and C, Figure 5—figure supplement 1), and all three variants caused a significantly larger number of cells to migrate.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 5B and C.

claim: CXCL12-induced chemotaxis in HeLa cells was dependent on the expression of P-Rex1.
source: CXCL12-induced chemotaxis was dependent on the expression of P-Rex1 (Figure 5B and C, Figure 5—figure supplement 1), and all three variants caused a significantly larger number of cells to migrate.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 5B and C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: EGF-induced chemotaxis in HeLa cells, which is not dependent on P-Rex1, was unaffected by P-Rex1 expression.
source: However, EGF-induced chemotaxis in HeLa cells, which is not dependent on P-Rex1, was unaffected by P-Rex1 expression.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 5B and C.

claim: The DH–DEP1 and PH–4HB interfaces of P-Rex1 mediate autoinhibition that specifically modulates chemokine-induced cell migration.
source: These data support that the DH–DEP1 and PH–4HB interfaces of P-Rex1 mediate autoinhibition that specifically modulates chemokine-induced cell migration.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the cell migration data in Figure 5.

claim: The PH domain would not be able to interact with PIP3 in a cell membrane while P-Rex1 is in its autoinhibited conformation.
source: Given the known binding site for Gβγ (Cash et al., 2019), the position of membrane-binding loops such as the β1/β2 loop of the DEP1 domain (Ravala et al., 2020), and the position of the 4HB domain, it does not seem that the PH domain would be able to interact with PIP3 in a cell membrane while P-Rex1 is in its autoinhibited conformation.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the structural data and citations to prior work.

claim: Without PIP3, the most notable changes in P-Rex1 in response to liposomes were increases in protection of the lipid binding elements of both DEP domains (primarily their β1/β2 loops).
source: Without PIP3, the most notable changes in P-Rex1 in response to liposomes were increases in protection of the lipid binding elements of both DEP domains (primarily their β1/β2 loops; Figure 6—figure supplement 1A), which suggests that they directly interact with lipid bilayers.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The DEP domains of P-Rex1 directly interact with lipid bilayers.
source: Without PIP3, the most notable changes in P-Rex1 in response to liposomes were increases in protection of the lipid binding elements of both DEP domains (primarily their β1/β2 loops; Figure 6—figure supplement 1A), which suggests that they directly interact with lipid bilayers.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on HDX-MS data in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The isolated DEP1 can independently bind negatively charged liposomes.
source: Indeed, the isolated DEP1 can independently bind negatively charged liposomes (Ravala et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation to prior work.

claim: Within the PH domain, there was deprotection of the αC helix in response to liposomes without PIP3.
source: Within the PH domain, there was deprotection of the αC helix, but there was no deprotection at the PH–4HB interface, suggesting that it remained intact.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on HDX-MS data in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: There was no deprotection at the PH–4HB interface in response to liposomes without PIP3, suggesting that it remained intact.
source: Within the PH domain, there was deprotection of the αC helix, but there was no deprotection at the PH–4HB interface, suggesting that it remained intact.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on HDX-MS data in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Membranes with PIP3 caused deprotection of the entire DH domain.
source: In contrast, membranes with PIP3 caused deprotection of the entire DH domain, the α6-αN linker and the helices at the DH–DEP1 interface (Figure 6A, Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Membranes with PIP3 caused deprotection of the α6-αN linker.
source: In contrast, membranes with PIP3 caused deprotection of the entire DH domain, the α6-αN linker and the helices at the DH–DEP1 interface (Figure 6A, Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Membranes with PIP3 caused deprotection of the helices at the DH–DEP1 interface.
source: In contrast, membranes with PIP3 caused deprotection of the entire DH domain, the α6-αN linker and the helices at the DH–DEP1 interface (Figure 6A, Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The core of the PH domain showed an increase in protection in the presence of PIP3.
source: Although the core of the PH domain showed, as expected, an increase in protection in the presence of PIP3, the structural elements contacting 4HB became deprotected, as did the PH-binding regions of 4HB.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on HDX-MS data in Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The structural elements of the PH domain contacting 4HB became deprotected in the presence of PIP3.
source: Although the core of the PH domain showed, as expected, an increase in protection in the presence of PIP3, the structural elements contacting 4HB became deprotected, as did the PH-binding regions of 4HB.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on HDX-MS data in Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The PH-binding regions of 4HB became deprotected in the presence of PIP3.
source: Although the core of the PH domain showed, as expected, an increase in protection in the presence of PIP3, the structural elements contacting 4HB became deprotected, as did the PH-binding regions of 4HB.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on HDX-MS data in Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The HDX-MS data are consistent with loosening of interdomain contacts and unraveling of at least some fraction of P-Rex1 onto the surface of the liposome.
source: Collectively, these data are consistent with loosening of interdomain contacts and unraveling of at least some fraction of P-Rex1 onto the surface of the liposome.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the HDX-MS data in Figure 6.

claim: IP4 can reduce P-Rex1 activity by stabilizing the autoinhibited conformation of the enzyme at physiologically relevant concentrations.
source: Surprisingly, we found that the PIP3 headgroup analog IP4 can reduce P-Rex1 activity by stabilizing the autoinhibited conformation of the enzyme at physiologically relevant concentrations, suggesting a previously unknown, additional mechanism of regulation.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion stated in the discussion based on the experimental data.

claim: P-Rex1 binding to PIP3-containing membranes induces conformational changes that unwind P-Rex1 into a fully active state.
source: Our experiments further suggest that P-Rex1 binding to PIP3-containing membranes induces conformational changes that unwind P-Rex1 into a fully active state.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion stated in the discussion based on the HDX-MS data in Figure 6.

claim: Inositol phosphates, including IP7 and IP4, can compete with PIP3 binding to PH domains.
source: Additionally, inositol phosphates, including IP7 and IP4, can compete with PIP3 binding to PH domains (Jia et al., 2007), representing another form of negative regulation.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a citation to prior work.

claim: Ins(1,3,4,5)P4 is a major isoform of IP4 in neutrophils.
source: Ins(1,3,4,5)P4 is a major isoform of IP4 in neutrophils (Stuart et al., 1994) where its concentration is estimated to be 4 μM (French et al., 1991) and where P-Rex1 is highly expressed (Welch et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations to prior work.

claim: The concentration of Ins(1,3,4,5)P4 in neutrophils is estimated to be 4 μM.
source: Ins(1,3,4,5)P4 is a major isoform of IP4 in neutrophils (Stuart et al., 1994) where its concentration is estimated to be 4 μM (French et al., 1991) and where P-Rex1 is highly expressed (Welch et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations to prior work.

claim: IP4 may exert biologically relevant control of Rac activation, at least in neutrophils.
source: Because we can measure robust inhibition of P-Rex1 by IP4 at >1 µM (Figure 1D), IP4 may exert biologically relevant control of Rac activation, at least in neutrophils.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the discussion based on the experimental data in Figure 1D and the known concentration of IP4 in neutrophils.

claim: P-Rex1 can bind membranes in the absence of PIP3 or Gβγ.
source: Because P-Rex1 can bind membranes in the absence of PIP3 or Gβγ, IP4 may also serve to suppress P-Rex1 activity until a threshold concentration of PIP3 is generated, allowing rapid activation of already membrane-associated P-Rex1.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an established fact.

claim: IP4 may serve to suppress P-Rex1 activity until a threshold concentration of PIP3 is generated, allowing rapid activation of already membrane-associated P-Rex1.
source: Because P-Rex1 can bind membranes in the absence of PIP3 or Gβγ, IP4 may also serve to suppress P-Rex1 activity until a threshold concentration of PIP3 is generated, allowing rapid activation of already membrane-associated P-Rex1.
evidence: This is a hypothesis stated in the discussion based on the experimental data.

claim: Regulation by specific inositol phosphates may depend on the intracellular distribution of the enzymes responsible for their synthesis.
source: It is worth noting that such regulation by specific inositol phosphates may depend on the intracellular distribution of the enzymes responsible for their synthesis (Gokhale et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a citation to prior work.

claim: Deletion of the PH domain in P-Rex1 resulted in a large increase in activity in the context of the full-length enzyme.
source: Nearly two decades ago, it was first reported that domains located C-terminal to the DH domain contribute to P-Rex1 autoinhibition (Hill et al., 2005). Deletion of the PH domain in P-Rex1 resulted in a large increase in activity in the context of the full-length enzyme.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a citation to prior work.

claim: The DH/PH fragment has higher activity than DH/PH-DEP1 and larger P-Rex1 fragments.
source: However, the DH/PH fragment has higher activity than DH/PH-DEP1 and larger P-Rex1 fragments, indicating that the PH domain itself is not intrinsically inhibitory, as it is in some other RhoGEF DH/PH tandems (Bandekar et al., 2019; Chen et al., 2020; Ravala and Tesmer, 2024).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations to prior work.

claim: The PH domain itself is not intrinsically inhibitory in P-Rex1, as it is in some other RhoGEF DH/PH tandems.
source: However, the DH/PH fragment has higher activity than DH/PH-DEP1 and larger P-Rex1 fragments, indicating that the PH domain itself is not intrinsically inhibitory, as it is in some other RhoGEF DH/PH tandems (Bandekar et al., 2019; Chen et al., 2020; Ravala and Tesmer, 2024).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations to prior work.

claim: In DH/PH-DEP1 and larger fragments, the DH/PH module can jack-knife and position the PH domain in a manner that blocks GTPase binding.
source: This apparent contradiction can now be explained by the fact that in DH/PH-DEP1 and larger fragments, the DH/PH module can jack-knife and position the PH domain in a manner that blocks GTPase binding.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the discussion based on the structural data.

claim: The isolated DEP1 domain plays an autoinhibitory role based on the relatively low activity of DH/PH-DEP1 relative to DH/PH.
source: The isolated DEP1 domain was also shown to play an autoinhibitory role based on the relatively low activity of DH/PH-DEP1 relative to DH/PH (Ravala et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a citation to prior work.

claim: The DEP1 domain positions the PH domain to block access of GTPases by its interaction with the DH domain.
source: This can now be explained by its interaction with the DH domain, which, consequently, positions the PH domain to block access of GTPases.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the discussion based on the structural data.

claim: The DH/PH-DEP1 module can be thought of as the core signaling circuit in P-Rex1.
source: Because the PH and DEP1 domains can mediate inhibition in the contexts of both DH/PH-DEP1 and the full-length enzyme, and because there is little GEF activity when the DH–DEP1 interface is intact, the DH/PH-DEP1 module can be thought of as the core signaling circuit in P-Rex1.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the discussion based on the experimental data.

claim: Mutations in the DH–DEP1 interface were, in general, more activating than those in the PH–4HB interface in cells.
source: In support of this, our mutations in the DH–DEP1 interface were, in general, more activating than those in the PH–4HB interface in cells, although we note that our mutagenesis was not exhaustive (Figure 5).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on the cell migration data in Figure 5.

claim: P-Rex1 in its basal state may be associated with IP4 and exist in equilibrium between the membrane and the cytosol.
source: P-Rex1 in its basal state may be associated with IP4 and exist in equilibrium between the membrane and the cytosol.
evidence: This is a hypothesis stated in the discussion based on the experimental data.

claim: In the autoinhibited configuration of P-Rex1, the known membrane anchoring elements cannot engage a common membrane plane.
source: In its autoinhibited configuration, the known membrane anchoring elements (the GTPase binding site of the DH domain, the PIP3-binding site of the PH domain, the β3/β4 loop of the PH domain, the β1/β2 loops of DEP1 and DEP2, and the Gβγ-binding site in the C-terminal domains) cannot engage a common membrane plane (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on the structural data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The PH domain would not be able to engage the membrane along with the other domains without unwrapping of the autoinhibited conformation.
source: The clear outlier is the PH domain that would not be able to engage the membrane along with the other domains without unwrapping of the autoinhibited conformation.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on the structural data.

claim: PIP3 is not a major driver of membrane anchoring on its own.
source: PIP3 is not a major driver of membrane anchoring on its own (Barber et al., 2007; Cash et al., 2016), and nor is Gβγ, but they do so synergistically in combination (Barber et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations to prior work.

claim: Gβγ is not a major driver of membrane anchoring on its own.
source: PIP3 is not a major driver of membrane anchoring on its own (Barber et al., 2007; Cash et al., 2016), and nor is Gβγ, but they do so synergistically in combination (Barber et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations to prior work.

claim: PIP3 and Gβγ synergistically drive membrane anchoring in combination.
source: PIP3 is not a major driver of membrane anchoring on its own (Barber et al., 2007; Cash et al., 2016), and nor is Gβγ, but they do so synergistically in combination (Barber et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations to prior work.

claim: Gβγ-binding did not have a large effect on the regions involved in autoinhibition in prior HDX-MS studies.
source: In prior HDX-MS studies, Gβγ-binding did not have a large effect on the regions now known to be involved in autoinhibition and only caused protection in regions of direct contact (Cash et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a citation to prior work.

claim: The role of Gβγ in activation may be primarily related to translocation.
source: This supports the idea that its role in activation may be primarily related to translocation.
evidence: This is a hypothesis stated in the discussion based on prior HDX-MS data.

claim: The ΔPH variant of P-Rex1 (which cannot form the DEP1–DH or PH–4HB interfaces or bind PIP3) is activated to the same extent by Gβγ as WT P-Rex1.
source: This is consistent with the observation that the ΔPH variant of P-Rex1 (which cannot form the DEP1–DH or PH–4HB interfaces or bind PIP3) is activated to the same extent by Gβγ as WT P-Rex1 (Hill et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a citation to prior work.

claim: In autoinhibited P-Rex1, the Gβγ-binding site is readily accessible whereas that of PIP3 is sequestered.
source: Furthermore, in autoinhibited P-Rex1, the Gβγ-binding site is readily accessible whereas that of PIP3 is sequestered.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on the structural data.

claim: After stimulation of GPCRs in neutrophils, Gβγ likely binds first.
source: We propose that, after stimulation of GPCRs in neutrophils, Gβγ likely binds first and, with the assistance of membrane binding elements in the DEP1 and 2 domains and possibly the β3/β4 loop of the PH domain, promotes loosening of the autoinhibited state (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a hypothesis stated in the discussion based on the experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Gβγ, with the assistance of membrane binding elements in the DEP1 and 2 domains and possibly the β3/β4 loop of the PH domain, promotes loosening of the autoinhibited state.
source: We propose that, after stimulation of GPCRs in neutrophils, Gβγ likely binds first and, with the assistance of membrane binding elements in the DEP1 and 2 domains and possibly the β3/β4 loop of the PH domain, promotes loosening of the autoinhibited state (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a hypothesis stated in the discussion based on the experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Generation of PIP3 by PI3K releases the DH/PH module from the 4HB and DEP1 domain, displacing any bound IP4.
source: Generation of PIP3 by PI3K then releases the DH/PH module from the 4HB and DEP1 domain, displacing any bound IP4.
evidence: This is a hypothesis stated in the discussion based on the experimental data.

claim: Neither PIP3 nor IP4 can activate DH/PH-DEP1 GEF activity on a soluble GTPase.
source: Because neither PIP3 nor IP4 can activate DH/PH-DEP1 GEF activity on a soluble GTPase (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), we speculate that this unwrapping at the membrane with multiple points of engagement across the protein is necessary for full activation of P-Rex1 (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Unwrapping at the membrane with multiple points of engagement across the protein is necessary for full activation of P-Rex1.
source: Because neither PIP3 nor IP4 can activate DH/PH-DEP1 GEF activity on a soluble GTPase (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), we speculate that this unwrapping at the membrane with multiple points of engagement across the protein is necessary for full activation of P-Rex1 (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a hypothesis stated in the discussion based on the experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and Figure 6B.

claim: Fully activated P-Rex1 at the membrane will be more extended and dynamic, rendering the DH domain more accessible to Rac1.
source: Indeed, our HDX-MS and SAXS studies here support that fully activated P-Rex1 at the membrane will be more extended and dynamic, rendering the DH domain more accessible to Rac1.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the discussion based on the HDX-MS and SAXS data.

claim: Phosphorylation of the lipid binding loop of DEP1 by PKA is known to inhibit P-Rex1.
source: For example, phosphorylation of the lipid binding loop of DEP1 by PKA is known to inhibit P-Rex1 (Chávez-Vargas et al., 2016; Ravala et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations to prior work.

claim: A potential interaction may occur between the basic β3/β4 loop of the PH domain and the loop at the end of the 4HB.
source: Also, a potential interaction may occur between the basic β3/β4 loop of the PH domain and the loop at the end of the 4HB (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a hypothesis stated in the discussion based on the structural data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Both the β3/β4 loop of the PH domain and the loop at the end of the 4HB have predicted and confirmed phosphorylation sites.
source: Both loops, consistent with their extended and dynamic nature, have predicted and confirmed phosphorylation sites (Barber et al., 2012) and thus could potentially modulate P-Rex1 activity if they interact.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a citation to prior work.

claim: Phosphorylation of the basic β3/β4 loop might be expected to inhibit activity based on the fact that it binds and localizes the protein to the negatively charged plasma membrane.
source: Phosphorylation of the basic β3/β4 loop might be expected to inhibit activity based on the fact that it binds and localizes the protein to the negatively charged plasma membrane, consistent with dephosphorylation of the loop leading to activation (Montero et al., 2016; Montero et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a hypothesis stated in the discussion with citations to prior work.

claim: Dephosphorylation of the β3/β4 loop leads to activation of P-Rex1.
source: Phosphorylation of the basic β3/β4 loop might be expected to inhibit activity based on the fact that it binds and localizes the protein to the negatively charged plasma membrane, consistent with dephosphorylation of the loop leading to activation (Montero et al., 2016; Montero et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations to prior work.
